paragraphs: Friend, here is the big idea: Christ already set you free, so STAND in it. "It is for freedom that Christ has set us free," Paul writes (Galatians 5:1). Trying to be justified by the law means trying to add to what Christ finished, and Paul says that cuts you off from Him (Galatians 5:4). You don't earn this freedom with sweat. You receive it, and by faith you "eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness" (Galatians 5:5).

So what does a free person look like? Paul says, "What matters is faith expressing itself through love" (Galatians 5:6). Freedom is not a permission slip to do whatever you feel like. Paul says do not use it "as an opportunity for the flesh," but "serve one another in love" (Galatians 5:13). And that one command holds the whole law: "Love your neighbor as yourself" (Galatians 5:14).

Now watch the little stuff, baker. Paul says "A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (Galatians 5:9), and I have ruined a batch or two that way, so I believe him. One small wrong idea about earning your place can spread through everything. And when people forget the love part, Paul warns that biting and devouring one another ends with being "consumed by one another" (Galatians 5:15). Hold on to Christ, stay free, and spend that freedom on the people right next to you.
